claim: The repo reports that ShadowOfWar.exe statically imports steam_api64.dll (shipped in x64\) and delay-loads d3d11.dll and amd_ags_x64.dll, making steam_api64.dll the chosen proxy injection point.
evidence: docs/reverse-engineering.md:71 "Delay-loaded imports (2): d3d11.dll, amd_ags_x64.dll"; :80 "leading candidate: proxy steam_api64.dll"
game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN: repo records no game version, Steam buildid, exe hash or build check; it only states a ~112 MB x64 Steam exe with SteamStub v3.1 + Denuvo (docs/reverse-engineering.md:12,21-29). Our exe is 117732784 bytes (~112.3 MiB), consistent but not proof of 1.0.8874.0 / build 3095001. Our install dir does contain steam_api64.dll and amd_ags_x64.dll, matching the repo's description.
verification_method: Static read of repo docs. Verify against our build by parsing the import and delay-import directories of our ShadowOfWar.exe (read-only PE parse).
limitations: Import table facts are the author's; not re-derived from our exe. Proxying steam_api64 may interact with SteamStub/Denuvo integrity checks - repo claims it worked live but gives no build id.
next_experiment: Read-only PE import parse of our ShadowOfWar.exe to confirm steam_api64.dll static import and the delay-load list.
